parsed.use_case: A configuration management service records historical revisions whenever an application setting or feature flag is updated. During post-incident debugging or replay analysis, the service must reliably determine which setting value was active at a specific past moment in time.
system_examples: Google Cloud Spanner — uses multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) to execute point-in-time stale reads by finding the most recent committed version of a cell at or prior to a client-specified timestamp.
Prometheus — evaluates instant queries by locating the most recent recorded sample for a metric time series occurring at or before the query evaluation timestamp within a lookback window.
Apache HBase — retains versioned cells ordered chronologically per row key and column, returning the latest value whose timestamp does not exceed the query's upper time boundary.
parsed.explanation: The standard solution combines a hash map pointing each key to a chronologically ordered array of entries, then uses binary search to find the predecessor timestamp. While a naive linear scan takes O(N) time per read across N versions, binary search reduces lookup latency to O(log N) while maintaining O(1) appends for monotonic timestamps. In production MVCC engines and time-series systems, this logarithmic retrieval ensures point-in-time queries remain fast even as version history grows into millions of entries.
